passages.text: In the third year of the reign of King Belshazzar, a vision appeared to me, Daniel, subsequent to the one that had appeared to me earlier.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet of God.
Daniel lived during the reign of King Belshazzar.
King Belshazzar was the ruler at that time.
In the third year of King Belshazzar’s reign, Daniel saw a vision.
This vision appeared to Daniel after he had seen an earlier vision.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַ֣ת שָׁל֔וֹשׁ לְמַלְכ֖וּת בֵּלְאשַׁצַּ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ חָז֞וֹן נִרְאָ֤ה אֵלַי֙ אֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֔אל אַחֲרֵ֛י הַנִּרְאָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י בַּתְּחִלָּֽה׃

passages.text: And in the vision I saw myself in the citadel of Susa, in the province of Elam. I saw in the vision that I was beside the Ulai Canal.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet.
Daniel lived during the reign of King Belshazzar.
Daniel received a vision from God.
In the vision, Daniel saw himself in the citadel of Susa.
Susa was a fortress city.
Susa was in the province of Elam.
Daniel saw himself standing beside the Ulai Canal.
Daniel saw all these things in his vision.
passages.original: וָֽאֶרְאֶה֮ בֶּחָזוֹן֒ וַיְהִי֙ בִּרְאֹתִ֔י וַאֲנִי֙ בְּשׁוּשַׁ֣ן הַבִּירָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵילָ֣ם הַמְּדִינָ֑ה וָאֶרְאֶה֙ בֶּֽחָז֔וֹן וַאֲנִ֥י הָיִ֖יתִי עַל־ אוּבַ֥ל אוּלָֽי׃

passages.text: Then I lifted up my eyes and saw a ram with two horns standing beside the canal. The horns were long, but one was longer than the other, and the longer one grew up later.
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a vision.
Daniel was beside the Ulai Canal.
Daniel looked up.
Daniel saw a ram.
The ram stood beside the canal.
The ram had two horns.
Both horns were long.
One horn was longer than the other.
The longer horn grew up after the other.
passages.original: וָאֶשָּׂ֤א עֵינַי֙ וָאֶרְאֶ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֣ה׀ אַ֣יִל אֶחָ֗ד עֹמֵ֛ד לִפְנֵ֥י הָאֻבָ֖ל וְל֣וֹ קְרָנָ֑יִם וְהַקְּרָנַ֣יִם גְּבֹה֗וֹת וְהָאַחַת֙ גְּבֹהָ֣ה מִן־ הַשֵּׁנִ֔ית וְהַ֨גְּבֹהָ֔ה עֹלָ֖ה בָּאַחֲרֹנָֽה׃

passages.text: I saw the ram charging toward the west and the north and the south. No animal could stand against him, and there was no deliverance from his power. He did as he pleased and became great.
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a ram in his vision.
The ram charged toward the west.
The ram charged toward the north.
The ram charged toward the south.
No animal could stand against the ram.
No one could rescue from the ram’s power.
The ram did whatever he wanted.
The ram became great.
passages.original: רָאִ֣יתִי אֶת־ הָאַ֡יִל מְנַגֵּחַ֩ יָ֨מָּה וְצָפ֜וֹנָה וָנֶ֗גְבָּה וְכָל־ חַיּוֹת֙ לֹֽא־ יַֽעַמְד֣וּ לְפָנָ֔יו וְאֵ֥ין מַצִּ֖יל מִיָּד֑וֹ וְעָשָׂ֥ה כִרְצֹנ֖וֹ וְהִגְדִּֽיל׃

passages.text: As I was contemplating all this, suddenly a goat with a prominent horn between his eyes came out of the west, crossing the surface of the entire earth without touching the ground.
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a vision.
Daniel was thinking about what he had seen.
Suddenly, a male goat appeared.
The goat came from the west.
The goat crossed over the whole earth.
The goat did not touch the ground.
The goat had a large, noticeable horn.
The horn was between the goat’s eyes.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֣י׀ הָיִ֣יתִי מֵבִ֗ין וְהִנֵּ֤ה צְפִיר־ הָֽעִזִּים֙ בָּ֤א מִן־ הַֽמַּעֲרָב֙ עַל־ פְּנֵ֣י כָל־ הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֵ֥ין נוֹגֵ֖עַ בָּאָ֑רֶץ וְהַ֨צָּפִ֔יר קֶ֥רֶן חָז֖וּת בֵּ֥ין עֵינָֽיו׃

passages.text: He came toward the two-horned ram I had seen standing beside the canal and rushed at him with furious power.
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a vision.
Daniel saw a ram with two horns.
The ram stood beside the canal.
A goat appeared in the vision.
The goat came toward the ram.
The goat rushed at the ram.
The goat attacked with furious power.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֗א עַד־ הָאַ֙יִל֙ בַּ֣עַל הַקְּרָנַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָאִ֔יתִי עֹמֵ֖ד לִפְנֵ֣י הָאֻבָ֑ל וַיָּ֥רָץ אֵלָ֖יו בַּחֲמַ֥ת כֹּחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: I saw him approach the ram in a rage against him, and he struck the ram and shattered his two horns. The ram was powerless to stand against him, and the goat threw him to the ground and trampled him, and no one could deliver the ram from his power.
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a goat with a prominent horn between its eyes.
The goat came near a ram with two horns.
The goat was angry at the ram.
The goat struck the ram.
The goat broke both of the ram’s horns.
The ram had no strength to stand against the goat.
The goat threw the ram to the ground.
The goat trampled the ram.
No one could rescue the ram from the goat’s power.
passages.original: וּרְאִיתִ֞יו מַגִּ֣יעַ׀ אֵ֣צֶל הָאַ֗יִל וַיִּתְמַרְמַ֤ר אֵלָיו֙ וַיַּ֣ךְ אֶת־ הָאַ֔יִל וַיְשַׁבֵּר֙ אֶת־ שְׁתֵּ֣י קְרָנָ֔יו וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה כֹ֛חַ בָּאַ֖יִל לַעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּשְׁלִיכֵ֤הוּ אַ֙רְצָה֙ וַֽיִּרְמְסֵ֔הוּ וְלֹא־ הָיָ֥ה מַצִּ֛יל לָאַ֖יִל מִיָּדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Thus the goat became very great, but at the height of his power, his large horn was broken off, and four prominent horns came up in its place, pointing toward the four winds of heaven.
passages.sermon:
The goat became very great.
He grew strong and powerful.
At the height of his power, his large horn broke off.
Four prominent horns grew in its place.
These four horns pointed toward the four winds of heaven.
passages.original: וּצְפִ֥יר הָעִזִּ֖ים הִגְדִּ֣יל עַד־ מְאֹ֑ד וּכְעָצְמ֗וֹ נִשְׁבְּרָה֙ הַקֶּ֣רֶן הַגְּדוֹלָ֔ה וַֽתַּעֲלֶ֜נָה חָז֤וּת אַרְבַּע֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יהָ לְאַרְבַּ֖ע רוּח֥וֹת הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

passages.text: From one of these horns a little horn emerged and grew extensively toward the south and the east and toward the Beautiful Land.
passages.sermon:
A little horn came out from one of the four horns.
This little horn began to grow larger.
It grew toward the south.
It grew toward the east.
It grew toward the Beautiful Land.
The Beautiful Land is Israel.
passages.original: וּמִן־ הָאַחַ֣ת מֵהֶ֔ם יָצָ֥א קֶֽרֶן־ אַחַ֖ת מִצְּעִירָ֑ה וַתִּגְדַּל־ יֶ֛תֶר אֶל־ הַנֶּ֥גֶב וְאֶל־ הַמִּזְרָ֖ח וְאֶל־ הַצֶּֽבִי׃

passages.text: It grew as high as the host of heaven, and it cast down some of the host and some of the stars to the earth, and trampled them.
passages.sermon:
A little horn appeared from one of the four horns.
This little horn grew very powerful.
It became as high as the host of heaven.
The host of heaven means the armies or angels of God.
The little horn threw down some of the host to the earth.
It also threw down some of the stars to the earth.
The little horn trampled on those it cast down.
passages.original: וַתִּגְדַּ֖ל עַד־ צְבָ֣א הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַתַּפֵּ֥ל אַ֛רְצָה מִן־ הַצָּבָ֥א וּמִן־ הַכּוֹכָבִ֖ים וַֽתִּרְמְסֵֽם׃

passages.text: It magnified itself, even to the Prince of the host; it removed His daily sacrifice and overthrew the place of His sanctuary.
passages.sermon:
A little horn appeared from one of the horns.
This little horn grew very great.
It became proud and exalted itself.
It exalted itself even against the Prince of the host.
The Prince of the host is God.
The little horn took away the daily sacrifice from God.
It threw down the place of God’s sanctuary.
passages.original: וְעַ֥ד שַֽׂר־ הַצָּבָ֖א הִגְדִּ֑יל וּמִמֶּ֙נּוּ֙ הֵרִים הַתָּמִ֔יד וְהֻשְׁלַ֖ךְ מְכ֥וֹן מִקְדָּשֽׁוֹ׃

passages.text: And in the rebellion, the host and the daily sacrifice were given over to the horn, and it flung truth to the ground and prospered in whatever it did.
passages.sermon:
A rebellion happened.
A powerful horn appeared.
The horn received control over the host.
The horn received control over the daily sacrifice.
The horn acted in wickedness.
The horn threw truth to the ground.
The horn succeeded in everything it did.
passages.original: וְצָבָ֛א תִּנָּתֵ֥ן עַל־ הַתָּמִ֖יד בְּפָ֑שַׁע וְתַשְׁלֵ֤ךְ אֱמֶת֙ אַ֔רְצָה וְעָשְׂתָ֖ה וְהִצְלִֽיחָה׃

passages.text: Then I heard a holy one speaking, and another holy one said to him, “How long until the fulfillment of the vision of the daily sacrifice, the rebellion that causes desolation, and the surrender of the sanctuary and of the host to be trampled?”
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a vision from God.
Daniel heard a holy one speaking.
Another holy one spoke to the first holy one.
The second holy one asked a question.
He said, “How long will this vision last?”
He asked about the daily sacrifice.
He asked about the rebellion that brings desolation.
He asked about the time when the sanctuary will be given over.
He asked about the host being trampled.”
passages.original: וָאֶשְׁמְעָ֥ה אֶֽחָד־ קָד֖וֹשׁ מְדַבֵּ֑ר וַיֹּאמֶר֩ אֶחָ֨ד קָד֜וֹשׁ לַפַּֽלְמוֹנִ֣י הַֽמְדַבֵּ֗ר עַד־ מָתַ֞י הֶחָז֤וֹן הַתָּמִיד֙ וְהַפֶּ֣שַׁע שֹׁמֵ֔ם תֵּ֛ת וְקֹ֥דֶשׁ וְצָבָ֖א מִרְמָֽס׃

passages.text: He said to me, “It will take 2,300 evenings and mornings; then the sanctuary will be properly restored.”
passages.sermon:
The angel spoke to Daniel.
He said, “The vision is about the sanctuary.”
The sanctuary will suffer for a set time.
This time will last for 2,300 evenings and mornings.
After this period, God will restore the sanctuary.
The sanctuary will be made right again.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֔י עַ֚ד עֶ֣רֶב בֹּ֔קֶר אַלְפַּ֖יִם וּשְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וְנִצְדַּ֖ק קֹֽדֶשׁ׃

passages.text: While I, Daniel, was watching the vision and trying to understand it, there stood before me one having the appearance of a man.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet of God.
Daniel saw a vision.
Daniel tried to understand the vision.
A figure appeared in front of Daniel.
This figure looked like a man.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י בִּרְאֹתִ֛י אֲנִ֥י דָנִיֵּ֖אל אֶת־ הֶחָז֑וֹן וָאֲבַקְשָׁ֣ה בִינָ֔ה וְהִנֵּ֛ה עֹמֵ֥ד לְנֶגְדִּ֖י כְּמַרְאֵה־ גָֽבֶר׃

passages.text: And I heard the voice of a man calling from between the banks of the Ulai: “Gabriel, explain the vision to this man.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a vision.
Daniel heard a man’s voice.
The man spoke from between the banks of the Ulai River.
The man called out to Gabriel.
The man told Gabriel to explain the vision.
The man wanted Gabriel to explain the vision to Daniel.
passages.original: וָאֶשְׁמַ֥ע קוֹל־ אָדָ֖ם בֵּ֣ין אוּלָ֑י וַיִּקְרָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר גַּבְרִיאֵ֕ל הָבֵ֥ן לְהַלָּ֖ז אֶת־ הַמַּרְאֶֽה׃

passages.text: As he came near to where I stood, I was terrified and fell facedown. “Son of man,” he said to me, “understand that the vision concerns the time of the end.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet.
Daniel saw a vision.
A figure with the appearance of a man came near Daniel.
The figure approached Daniel where he stood.
Daniel became terrified.
Daniel fell facedown on the ground.
The figure spoke to Daniel.
The figure called Daniel "son of man."
The figure told Daniel to understand the vision.
The figure said the vision concerns the time of the end.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹא֙ אֵ֣צֶל עָמְדִ֔י וּבְבֹא֣וֹ נִבְעַ֔תִּי וָאֶפְּלָ֖ה עַל־ פָּנָ֑י וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלַי֙ הָבֵ֣ן בֶּן־ אָדָ֔ם כִּ֖י לְעֶת־ קֵ֥ץ הֶחָזֽוֹן׃

passages.text: While he was speaking with me, I fell into a deep sleep, with my face to the ground. Then he touched me, helped me to my feet, and said, “Behold, I will make known to you what will happen in the latter time of wrath, because it concerns the appointed time of the end.
passages.sermon:
Gabriel is an angel.
Gabriel spoke with me.
While Gabriel spoke, I fell into a deep sleep.
My face was on the ground.
Gabriel touched me.
Gabriel helped me stand up.
Gabriel said, “I will tell you what will happen in the last time of wrath.
These things will happen at the appointed time of the end.”
passages.original: וּבְדַבְּר֣וֹ עִמִּ֔י נִרְדַּ֥מְתִּי עַל־ פָּנַ֖י אָ֑רְצָה וַיִּ֨גַּע־ בִּ֔י וַיַּֽעֲמִידֵ֖נִי עַל־ עָמְדִֽי׃ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ הִנְנִ֣י מוֹדִֽיעֲךָ֔ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ יִהְיֶ֖ה בְּאַחֲרִ֣ית הַזָּ֑עַם כִּ֖י לְמוֹעֵ֥ד קֵֽץ׃

passages.text: The two-horned ram that you saw represents the kings of Media and Persia.
passages.sermon:
Daniel saw a ram in his vision.
This ram had two horns.
The ram represents two kings.
These kings rule Media and Persia.
passages.original: הָאַ֥יִל אֲשֶׁר־ רָאִ֖יתָ בַּ֣עַל הַקְּרָנָ֑יִם מַלְכֵ֖י מָדַ֥י וּפָרָֽס׃

passages.text: The shaggy goat represents the king of Greece, and the large horn between his eyes is the first king.
passages.sermon:
The shaggy goat is a symbol.
This symbol means the king of Greece.
The goat has a large horn between its eyes.
This large horn means the first king of Greece.
passages.original: וְהַצָּפִ֥יר הַשָּׂעִ֖יר מֶ֣לֶךְ יָוָ֑ן וְהַקֶּ֤רֶן הַגְּדוֹלָה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּין־ עֵינָ֔יו ה֖וּא הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ הָרִאשֽׁוֹן׃

passages.text: The four horns that replaced the broken one represent four kingdoms that will rise from that nation, but will not have the same power.
passages.sermon:
The four horns replaced the broken horn.
These four horns represent four kingdoms.
These four kingdoms will rise from that nation.
These four kingdoms will not have the same power as the first.
passages.original: וְהַ֨נִּשְׁבֶּ֔רֶת וַתַּֽעֲמֹ֥דְנָה אַרְבַּ֖ע תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ אַרְבַּ֧ע מַלְכֻי֛וֹת מִגּ֥וֹי יַעֲמֹ֖דְנָה וְלֹ֥א בְכֹחֽוֹ׃

passages.text: In the latter part of their reign, when the rebellion has reached its full measure, an insolent king, skilled in intrigue, will come to the throne.
passages.sermon:
Four kingdoms will rise from Greece.
These kingdoms will not have the same power as the first king.
In the latter part of their reign, the people will become very rebellious.
When the rebellion is complete, a new king will appear.
This king will be harsh and bold.
He will have a strong and insolent face.
He will be skilled at solving riddles and understanding mysteries.
He will come to power after the rebellion has grown full.
passages.original: וּֽבְאַחֲרִית֙ מַלְכוּתָ֔ם כְּהָתֵ֖ם הַפֹּשְׁעִ֑ים יַעֲמֹ֛ד מֶ֥לֶךְ עַז־ פָּנִ֖ים וּמֵבִ֥ין חִידֽוֹת׃

passages.text: His power will be great, but it will not be his own. He will cause terrible destruction and succeed in whatever he does. He will destroy the mighty men along with the holy people.
passages.sermon:
A king will rise who is insolent and skilled in intrigue.
His power will become very great.
This power will not come from himself.
He will cause terrible destruction.
He will succeed in everything he does.
He will destroy powerful people.
He will also destroy the holy people.
passages.original: וְעָצַ֤ם כֹּחוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א בְכֹח֔וֹ וְנִפְלָא֥וֹת יַשְׁחִ֖ית וְהִצְלִ֣יחַ וְעָשָׂ֑ה וְהִשְׁחִ֥ית עֲצוּמִ֖ים וְעַם־ קְדֹשִֽׁים׃

passages.text: Through his craft and by his hand, he will cause deceit to prosper, and in his own mind he will make himself great. In a time of peace he will destroy many, and he will even stand against the Prince of princes. Yet he will be broken off, but not by human hands.
passages.sermon:
An insolent king will rise to power.
He will be skilled in intrigue.
He will use his intelligence to succeed at deception.
He will make deceit prosper by his own actions.
He will think highly of himself in his heart.
He will make himself great in his own mind.
He will destroy many people during a time of peace.
He will oppose the Prince of princes.
No human hand will break him.
He will be broken without human effort.
passages.original: וְעַל־ שִׂכְל֗וֹ וְהִצְלִ֤יחַ מִרְמָה֙ בְּיָד֔וֹ וּבִלְבָב֣וֹ יַגְדִּ֔יל וּבְשַׁלְוָ֖ה יַשְׁחִ֣ית רַבִּ֑ים וְעַ֤ל־ שַׂר־ שָׂרִים֙ יַעֲמֹ֔ד וּבְאֶ֥פֶס יָ֖ד יִשָּׁבֵֽר׃

passages.text: The vision of the evenings and the mornings that has been spoken is true. Now you must seal up the vision, for it concerns the distant future.”
passages.sermon:
Daniel received a vision from God.
The vision described events of evenings and mornings.
God said this vision is true.
God commanded Daniel to seal up the vision.
This vision is for the distant future.
passages.original: וּמַרְאֵ֨ה הָעֶ֧רֶב וְהַבֹּ֛קֶר אֲשֶׁ֥ר נֶאֱמַ֖ר אֱמֶ֣ת ה֑וּא וְאַתָּה֙ סְתֹ֣ם הֶֽחָז֔וֹן כִּ֖י לְיָמִ֥ים רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: I, Daniel, was exhausted and lay ill for days. Then I got up and went about the king’s business. I was confounded by the vision; it was beyond understanding.
passages.sermon:
Daniel was a prophet in Babylon.
Daniel saw a vision from God.
The vision troubled Daniel.
Daniel became exhausted.
Daniel lay sick for several days.
After some days, Daniel got up.
Daniel returned to his work for the king.
Daniel was still astonished by the vision.
Daniel could not understand the vision.
passages.original: וַאֲנִ֣י דָנִיֵּ֗אל נִהְיֵ֤יתִי וְנֶֽחֱלֵ֙יתִי֙ יָמִ֔ים וָאָק֕וּם וָאֶֽעֱשֶׂ֖ה אֶת־ מְלֶ֣אכֶת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וָאֶשְׁתּוֹמֵ֥ם עַל־ הַמַּרְאֶ֖ה וְאֵ֥ין מֵבִֽין׃פ
